selection_purpose: Small, shared farther-and-higher change with less early amplification; not best measured accuracy

reviewed.scope: All 24 IDs and all ten real future times for primary constant/late choices and CV; not every generated candidate movie watched in full

groups.0: Late placing bend to the right is already premature. Expansion raises/extends it but cannot restore the observed vertical lift.
groups.1: Vertical lift remains coherent. Constant scale leads the cup upward early; delayed expansion leaves the first second intact.
groups.2: Same early vertical lead. Larger late extent can put endpoints above the reference; expansion is not uniformly beneficial.

cup.conclusion: Use the delayed small expansion to demonstrate the requested shape change; retain original x1/3 and CV as accuracy controls.

groups.0: Rightward arc begins too soon. Extra height improves some final positions; delayed expansion avoids increasing the first-second lead.
groups.1: Similar early bend toward pot; endpoints can move closer with the small height shift.
groups.2: Wider curve and larger endpoint discrepancy persist; raising scale hurts this group despite gains in the other groups.

bottle.conclusion: Shared late expansion modestly improves global endpoint error, while average error remains slightly worse than x1/3.

rejected.scale_040_and_042: Amplify premature motion and widen arcs too strongly for a slight shared change
rejected.constant_scale_036_lift005: Same final extent as selected schedule but visibly larger early lead
rejected.independent_per_scene_tuning: Not used; both scenes share the same K and rule

limitations: AugE K is a calibration hypothesis
Tracker reference is not manual ground truth
Greedy genuine model forecasts are reused; this is postprocessing
H3 5 FPS versus documented F30 15 FPS remains a temporal shift
Same two previously inspected scenes, not independent test evaluation
Common smoothing Z is retained from prior CASE-AUGE ray-only control
